findings.title: XSS via unescaped URL interpolation in imported_from link
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import builds an HTML anchor by interpolating the attacker-controlled `url` parameter directly into an href attribute and link text: `"#{url}"`. The url is only checked with a loose regex (`/^https?\:\/\//`) and is never HTML-escaped. A URL such as `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` or one containing `'>

findings.title: Raw HTML from external feeds stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. In app/models/post.rb (lines 130-137), `cook` short-circuits and returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing the entire Markdown pipeline and Sanitize-based HTML cleaning that normally applies to all user content. The `contents` come straight from an external RSS/Atom feed (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or from a remote page fetched by ruby-readability (import_remote, line 48). Any script, event handler, or iframe in the feed content is persisted verbatim into `posts.cooked` and rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19 and in the standard topic view. This allows a compromised or malicious feed (feed_polling_url is an admin setting, but embed_url values come from third-party sites via the public /embed/best endpoint) to inject arbitrary JavaScript into the forum — a stored XSS. Imported HTML must be passed through Sanitize with a whitelist before being stored.

findings.title: Referer host check compares against embeddable_host, allowing any path on that host and being spoofable
findings.body: ensure_embeddable validates only that `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Two problems: (1) The Referer header is fully client-controlled — an attacker can send any Referer (or a page on the allowed host can be an open redirect / contain attacker content), so this check does not actually prove the embed is on the configured site; combined with `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` (line 28) this lets any third-party page iframe the endpoint. (2) The comparison is exact-host equality, so `evil-eviltrout.com.attacker.com` style suffixes fail but subdomains like `anything.eviltrout.com` pass if embeddable_host is a registrable domain, and conversely if embeddable_host is set to a bare hostname any subdomain matches. More importantly, the check should validate that the referer's host is the configured host (or a subdomain of it) AND that the embed_url host matches the same configured host — currently embed_url is never validated against embeddable_host in the controller, so the controller will happily enqueue retrieval of arbitrary URLs (see TopicRetriever, which does check, but only inside the job). The referer check should be a suffix match on the registrable domain and the embed_url should be validated server-side in the controller before enqueueing.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL is not a valid header value and disables framing protection
findings.body: The controller sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. ALLOWALL is not a recognized X-Frame-Options directive (valid values are DENY and SAMEORIGIN); browsers ignore unknown directives, so this header provides no protection and, worse, signals intent to allow framing from anywhere. Since the endpoint renders user-generated post content (including the unsanitized raw_html posts created by TopicEmbed), any site can embed it. If framing from the configured host only is intended, the correct approach is to omit X-Frame-Options and rely on CSP `frame-ancestors`, or set it conditionally. At minimum the invalid value should be removed or replaced with a real mechanism.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses indexOf substring match, which is bypassable
findings.body: The message handler validates the sender with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring check: if discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com`, then origins like `https://forum.example.com.evil.com`, `https://evil.com/?x=forum.example.com`, or `https://notforum.example.com` (contains the string) all pass the check. A malicious page can therefore post a `discourse-resize` message and set the iframe height to an arbitrary value (e.g. a huge height to break the host page layout, or 0 to hide content). The check must be an exact origin comparison: `if (e.origin !== discourseUrl) { return; }` (after normalizing discourseUrl to an origin).

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the raw Referer header, enabling message leak to attacker-controlled origins
findings.body: The layout sends the resize message with `parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The targetOrigin is the full Referer URL supplied by the client. If the page is somehow framed by an attacker (see the ALLOWALL / referer-check findings), the height data is sent to that origin; more subtly, per the postMessage spec a full URL targetOrigin is matched against the origin, but using a client-controlled header as targetOrigin is fragile and, combined with the missing/invalid X-Frame-Options, means the only thing standing between an attacker and receiving these messages is the referer check. Additionally, `request.referer` is interpolated into a JavaScript string literal without escaping — a Referer containing a quote or `</script>` would break out of the script context (reflected XSS in the embed frame). The targetOrigin should be a fixed, server-derived origin (the configured embeddable host), and the value must be JS-escaped (e.g. via `json_escape` / `javascript_tag`).

findings.title: raw post.cooked rendered in embed view
findings.body:
The view renders `
<%= raw post.cooked %>
`. In the main Discourse UI, cooked post HTML is produced by the Markdown pipeline which sanitizes dangerous markup; here `raw` bypasses any escaping. For posts created through TopicEmbed this cooked content is entirely unsanitized external HTML (see the TopicEmbed raw_html finding), so any script in an imported article executes in the context of the Discourse origin inside the embed iframe. Even for normal cooked posts, re-rendering with `raw` in a separate layout that lacks the standard CSP/onebox protections weakens the XSS posture. The embed view should render cooked content through the same sanitization used elsewhere, and imported raw_html posts must never reach this template unsanitized.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string via <<
findings.body: Line 13 does `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the String object passed in by the caller. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35 the content is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` — a fresh string, so it's mostly harmless there, but in app/models/topic_embed.rb import_remote line 52, `doc.content` (the Readability result) is passed and then mutated; any caller reusing the string (e.g. computing the sha1 before/after, or the Disqus importer in lib/tasks/disqus.thor) will see the appended footer. Note also that `content_sha1` on line 16 is computed AFTER the mutation, so the stored hash includes the footer — meaning an update comparison is consistent, but the mutation of a caller-owned object is a hidden side effect that can corrupt data if the same string is reused (e.g. the spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb line 40 calls import twice with different literals, masking the issue). Use `contents = contents + ...` or `<<` on a dup.

findings.title: Check-then-act race in TopicEmbed.import allows duplicate topics for the same URL
findings.body: import does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, creates a topic/post/TopicEmbed inside a transaction. There is a unique index on embed_url (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb line 11), but the existence check happens before the transaction and outside any locking, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g. PollFeed running hourly while a user hits /embed/best and enqueues RetrieveTopic, or two Sidekiq workers) can both see `embed.blank?`, both create topics, and the second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique — leaving an orphaned topic+post created by PostCreator (the transaction wraps it, so it rolls back, but the failure is unhandled and the job has retry: false in poll_feed.rb line 12, so the item is silently lost). The correct pattern is to attempt the create and rescue RecordNotUnique, or lock/upsert. At minimum the job should handle the race gracefully.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on malformed feed or missing item fields; retry disabled means items are lost
findings.body: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a blocking, unvalidated HTTP fetch with no timeout, no error handling, and no content-type check; `rss.items.each` then dereferences `i.link`, `i.id`, `i.content` without nil checks. A feed that is temporarily down, returns HTML instead of RSS, or has an item without content raises an exception. Because the job declares `sidekiq_options retry: false` (line 12), the exception kills the run and the hourly recurrence simply tries again next hour — but any transient failure also means the whole feed is skipped, and `open()` on an `https` URL with a bad cert, or a redirect loop, will hang the Sidekiq worker indefinitely (no open-uri timeout/redirect limit). The job should rescue parse/network errors, use a timeout, and validate item fields before calling TopicEmbed.import.

findings.body:
`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` unescapes HTML entities in the feed content before it is stored as raw_html. RSS content is already HTML (often entity-encoded, e.g. `<p>` for a literal `

` in a code sample, or `&` for a literal `&`). Unescaping turns `<script>` into a real `

findings.title: feed_key is defined but never used — Last-Modified/ETag caching is dead code
findings.body: The job defines `feed_key` (a Redis key `feed-modified:<sha1 of url>`) but nothing in the file ever reads or writes it. The apparent intent was to send If-Modified-Since / track the feed's Last-Modified header and skip re-parsing unchanged feeds, but `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` every hour and re-imports every item (TopicEmbed.import does dedupe by content_sha1, so it's not catastrophic, but every item's content is re-hashed and compared each hour, and the HTTP fetch always happens). Either implement the conditional GET using feed_key or remove the dead method; as written it misleads maintainers into thinking conditional requests are happening.

findings.title: invalid_host? returns true when embeddable_host is blank, but comparison is exact-host and case-sensitive
findings.body: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` compares the configured host string directly to the URI host. If embeddable_host is configured as `http://eviltrout.com` (with scheme) or `Eviltrout.com` (mixed case) or `eviltrout.com/` (trailing slash), the comparison fails for perfectly valid embed URLs and retrieval is silently skipped; conversely `www.eviltrout.com` vs `eviltrout.com` mismatches. The setting is documented as "Host that can embed the comments" (config/locales/server.en.yml), so it should be normalized (strip scheme, downcase, strip port) before comparison, and the embed_url host should be compared as a suffix of the configured registrable domain. As written, misconfiguration silently disables the entire feature.

findings.title: Calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside RetrieveTopic defeats the purpose of the async job and can recurse
findings.body: perform_retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when feed polling is enabled. RetrieveTopic is itself a Sidekiq job enqueued from the embed controller; running the entire hourly feed poll synchronously inside it means a single embed request can trigger a full feed fetch and import of every item, blocking the RetrieveTopic worker for a long time (PollFeed does unbounded HTTP fetches with no timeout). Worse, PollFeed imports items via TopicEmbed.import, which is fine, but if any code path enqueues RetrieveTopic from within PollFeed processing there is potential for long chains; more practically, the design intent (per the class comment "First check RSS if that is enabled") is to check whether the feed already contains the URL, not to run the whole poll. This should instead query the feed (or a cached copy) for the specific embed_url, or enqueue PollFeed asynchronously and return, letting the loading page's 30-second reload pick up the result.

findings.title: fetch_http performs an unvalidated server-side request to a user-influenced URL (SSRF surface)
findings.body: fetch_http calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48). The URL originates from the `embed_url` query parameter of the public `/embed/best` endpoint (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 9). The only validation is `invalid_host?`, which checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This still allows SSRF-style abuse within the allowed host (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com:22/`, `http://eviltrout.com/admin/internal-endpoint`, `http://user:pass@eviltrout.com/`, or `file://` if the host string is ever misconfigured to match), and `open()` follows redirects by default, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (cloud metadata) or an internal service will be fetched and its content imported as a post. open-uri must be restricted: validate scheme is http/https, resolve and reject private/loopback/link-local IPs, disable redirects or re-validate each hop, and set timeouts.

findings.title: import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs with open() — no scheme, redirect, or private-network restrictions
findings.body: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` uses Kernel#open (open-uri) on a URL that, via TopicRetriever/RetrieveTopic, is ultimately derived from the public embed_url parameter, and via PollFeed from feed item links/ids (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` in poll_feed.rb line 33 — note this fallback accepts ANY string as a URL, including `file:///etc/passwd`, which open-uri will happily open). There is no scheme whitelist, no redirect limit, no timeout, and no protection against requests to internal/private IP ranges. This is a full SSRF primitive: an attacker who can influence a feed item id/link (or an embed_url on the allowed host that redirects) can make the server read local files (`file://`) or internal HTTP services and import the response body as a forum post, leaking internal data. The fetch must be hardened (scheme whitelist, redirect re-validation, IP range blocking, timeouts).

findings.title: Feed item id used as URL without any validation enables file:// and internal URL fetch
findings.body: `url = i.link; url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`. When an RSS item has no link (or a non-http link), the item's `id` (often a GUID, which in many feeds is a URN like `urn:uuid:...`, a tag URI, or — in attacker-controlled feeds — an arbitrary string such as `file:///etc/passwd` or `http://169.254.169.254/`) is used as the URL and passed to TopicEmbed.import → import_remote → `open(url)`. TopicEmbed.import line 11 does check `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and returns nil otherwise, which blocks file:// at that layer — but only for the import path; the regex is also loose (matches `https://` anywhere at the start, accepts `https://` followed by anything). The deeper issue is that poll_feed hands unvalidated feed data to a URL fetcher; the id fallback should be removed or strictly validated, and the fetch layer must enforce scheme/IP restrictions regardless (defense in depth).

findings.title: RetrieveTopic job is enqueued on every cache miss with no deduplication, enabling job flooding
findings.body: When no TopicEmbed exists for the embed_url, the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders the loading page, which auto-reloads every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb line 10). Each reload re-enters `best`, finds no embed (the job may still be running or throttled), and enqueues another RetrieveTopic job. TopicRetriever has a 60-second Redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?`), but that only prevents the actual fetch — the jobs still pile up in Sidekiq, and each one performs DB queries and, for staff users (`no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`), bypasses the throttle entirely. A popular embed (or a bot hitting /embed/best?embed_url=... directly with a valid Referer) can enqueue thousands of jobs. The controller should check the throttle key (or use a single enqueue-per-URL lock) before enqueueing, and the loading page should back off.

findings.title: TopicView is built with current_user, leaking private topic data into the public embed
findings.body: `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` passes the current user. The embed endpoint is meant to be loaded in an iframe on a third-party site; the iframe request will typically carry the Discourse session cookie of whatever user happens to view the host page (cookies are sent on iframe requests depending on SameSite settings). If that user is a staff member or a member of a restricted category, TopicView will include posts/topics they can see but anonymous visitors cannot, and the rendered HTML (including post content from restricted categories) is served to the third-party page. The embed view must always be built as an anonymous/system user (e.g. `TopicView.new(topic_id, nil, ...)` or a dedicated embed user) and should verify the topic is publicly visible before rendering. As written, restricted/private post content can be exfiltrated by embedding a URL.

findings.title: Update path revises the post but never updates the topic title
findings.body: When content changes, import revises the post via PostRevisor with the new contents, but the topic title (from the feed item's `i.title`) is never updated — only the initial creation uses `title`. A feed that renames an article leaves the Discourse topic with the stale original title forever. Additionally, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` skips validations/callbacks (acceptable here) but if the PostRevisor revision fails silently (revise! returns false when raw is unchanged — though sha1 differs so raw differs — or raises), the sha1 is still updated only after revise! returns, which is correct, but there is no transaction wrapping the revise + update_column, so a crash between them leaves the post updated but the sha1 stale, causing a redundant re-revision next poll (harmless but noisy). The title update is the real gap: PollFeed passes `i.title` on every run but import ignores it on the update path.

findings.title: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs and mishandles protocol-relative and default ports
findings.body: absolutize_urls rewrites only hrefs/srcs that `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`) and scheme-relative paths (`http://other.com/...` is fine, but `//host/path` is left as-is and will resolve against the Discourse origin when rendered, breaking images/links). Also, the port logic `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` appends the port for https URLs on port 80 or http URLs on port 443 incorrectly (e.g. `https://host:80/` would get `:80` appended even though URI normalizes... actually URI keeps explicit ports, so `https://eviltrout.com:80/` yields prefix `https://eviltrout.com:80` which is wrong-ish but functional). More importantly, relative URLs like `images/foo.jpg` (no leading slash) are not absolutized at all and will 404 when rendered from the Discourse origin. The method should use URI.join semantics for all relative references, not just root-relative ones.

findings.title: Avatar img src uses ERB interpolation inside a single-quoted HTML attribute without escaping
findings.body: `` interpolates the avatar URL into a single-quoted attribute with no HTML escaping. small_avatar_url is derived from the user's uploaded avatar or gravatar; an admin/user-controlled avatar URL containing a single quote would break out of the attribute. Rails' `image_tag` (used correctly on lines 8 and 26) escapes properly; this raw img tag should use `image_tag(post.user.small_avatar_url)` or at least `h()` the value. Low severity because avatar URLs are largely system-generated, but it's an inconsistency with the rest of the file and a latent injection point if avatar URLs ever become user-supplied strings.

findings.title: Controller spec expects TopicRetriever to be used, but the controller enqueues a job instead
findings.body: The test "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" stubs `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but the controller (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15) never calls TopicRetriever directly — it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The spec would fail against the actual implementation (TopicRetriever.new is never invoked in the controller), meaning either the spec is wrong or the controller was changed after the spec was written and the test suite is red. A correct test would expect `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (or `Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, ...)`). This is exactly the kind of spec that gives false confidence — it documents an implementation that doesn't exist.

findings.title: Update-path spec doesn't verify the content_sha1 changed or that a revision was created
findings.body: The "Supports updating the post" test only asserts `post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/`. It doesn't verify that the TopicEmbed's content_sha1 was updated (so the next poll with the same content won't re-revise), that a PostRevision was created, or that the returned post is the same post (same id) as the original. A regression where import creates a second topic on update (the race condition described in the concurrency finding) would still pass this test as long as cooked contains the new text. The test should assert `post.id == original_post.id`, `TopicEmbed.count == 1`, and the updated sha1.

findings.title: discourse_expires_in 1.minute is applied even to the loading page, causing rapid re-fetch churn
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` sets a 1-minute HTTP cache on both the rendered topic view and the loading page. For the loading page this is mostly harmless, but combined with the 30-second auto-reload in loading.html.erb, a shared/CDN cache could serve a stale loading page for up to a minute after the topic has actually been imported, making the embed appear stuck. More importantly, caching the rendered best view for only 1 minute means every embed impression after the first minute hits the Rails stack and rebuilds a TopicView (an expensive operation) — for a high-traffic embed this is a significant load multiplier. The cache duration should be longer for the success path (the content changes only when the topic changes) and the loading page should send no-cache headers so the reload actually re-queries.

findings.title: no_throttle is granted based on the user_id passed from the controller, which is the iframe viewer's identity
findings.body: `TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))` — the user_id comes from `current_user.try(:id)` in the embed controller, i.e. whichever Discourse user's browser loaded the third-party page. Any staff member who visits a page containing an embed (or an attacker who socially engineers a staff member to a page with many distinct embed_urls) gets the 60-second throttle disabled, allowing unbounded fetch/import of arbitrary URLs on the allowed host. The throttle bypass should not be tied to the viewer's identity at all; if staff bypass is desired it should be a server-side decision, and the throttle key should also incorporate the URL (it does) but the bypass should be removed or gated on a server-controlled flag.

findings.title: cook_method default of 1 does not match Post.cook_methods enum ordering
findings.body: The migration sets `default: 1, null: false` for posts.cook_method. Post.cook_methods is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (app/models/post.rb lines 63-65). Discourse's Enum assigns values starting at 1 in declaration order (regular=1, raw_html=2) — so default 1 = regular, which is correct. However, this is fragile: the migration hardcodes the integer 1 instead of referencing the enum, and the schema comment in post.rb doesn't list cook_method at all (the annotate block at the bottom of post.rb is missing the new column). If the enum order ever changes, existing rows silently change meaning. The migration should use a comment documenting the mapping, and the model's schema annotation should be regenerated to include cook_method. More importantly, `Post#cook` (line 133) compares `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` — for legacy rows defaulted to 1 this is regular, fine, but there's no DB check constraint tying the value to the enum, so a bad value (0, 3) silently falls through to the regular cook path.

findings.title: cook_method raw_html bypasses all cooking/sanitization with no guard on who can set it
findings.body: `cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The only setter is PostCreator line 216 (`post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method] if @opts[:cook_method].present?`), and PostCreator is a public API used by controllers with user-supplied opts in many places. Any code path that passes user-controlled opts through to PostCreator (e.g. a plugin, the API, or a future controller) can set cook_method to raw_html and store arbitrary unsanitized HTML. There is no Guardian check restricting raw_html to staff/import contexts. The raw_html path should be gated (e.g. only settable when the acting user is staff or via an explicit import flag checked against the guardian), and the value should be validated against the enum on assignment.

findings.title: skip_validations option now skips post validations on revise, but the raw_html cook_method is never re-applied on revision
findings.body: The diff changes `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which is needed for the import update path. However, when TopicEmbed.import revises a raw_html post (topic_embed.rb line 36), PostRevisor.update_post sets `@post.raw = @new_raw` and saves; the before_save callback in post.rb (line 321) recomputes `self.cooked = cook(raw, ...)` only `unless new_record?` — for an existing raw_html post, cook returns raw, so cooked is correctly set to the new raw. That part works. The subtle issue: `skip_validations` now bypasses Validators::PostValidator for ALL revisions when the option is passed, including length/entropy/spam checks — acceptable for the import path, but the option is a general-purpose footgun now available to any caller of PostRevisor. It should be named/scoped to the import use case or documented. Low severity since only TopicEmbed passes it today.

findings.title: Loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s with no cap, hammering the server for never-imported URLs
findings.body: The loading view does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000)` with no maximum retry count and no backoff. If the URL can never be imported (host not actually embeddable, fetch fails, user not found — TopicRetriever.fetch_http returns silently if embed_by_username is blank), the iframe reloads forever, each time enqueueing another RetrieveTopic job (see the controller finding). A single abandoned embed tab generates 2 requests/minute indefinitely plus a Sidekiq job each time. The reload should stop after N attempts and show a permanent message with a link to start the discussion on the forum.

findings.title: Embed route has no rate limiting and is unauthenticated
findings.body: `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` is a public, unauthenticated route with no rate limit. Combined with the job-enqueue-per-miss behavior and the TopicView construction on hit, it's an easy DoS/amplification vector: an attacker can request /embed/best?embed_url=<unique-string> with a spoofed Referer matching embeddable_host, each request enqueuing a Sidekiq job and (for existing topics) building a full TopicView. There is no RateLimiter usage in EmbedController. The endpoint should be rate limited per IP (and per embed_url), and the referer check should be supplemented with a per-IP limiter since the Referer is trivially spoofable.

findings.title: URL validation regex is too loose and inconsistent with the rest of the codebase
findings.body: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` accepts strings like `https://` (nothing after), `https://?x`, `https:// evil.com`, and `https://example.com/redirect?to=javascript:...`. It also uses escaped colons (`\:`) which are unnecessary in a regex. Elsewhere the codebase uses the same loose pattern (poll_feed.rb line 33), so the inconsistency is systemic, but the import path is the security boundary: a URL like `https://eviltrout.com@evil.com/` (userinfo trick) passes the regex and URI parsing will treat evil.com as the host — which then fails invalid_host? in TopicRetriever, but TopicEmbed.import is also called directly from PollFeed with feed-supplied URLs that bypass TopicRetriever's host check entirely. The URL should be parsed with URI() and validated: scheme in [http, https], host present, and host matching the expected domain.

findings.title: PollFeed spec requires the wrong dependency and never tests poll_feed itself
findings.body: The spec requires `jobs/regular/process_post` (line 2) — an unrelated job — instead of `jobs/scheduled/poll_feed`, and all four tests only exercise the `execute` guard conditions by mocking `poll_feed`. There is no test that poll_feed actually parses a feed, handles a missing user, handles a malformed feed, or calls TopicEmbed.import with the right arguments. The require of process_post suggests a copy-paste error and means the spec may not even load the class under test in some configurations. The spec should require the correct file and include tests for poll_feed's behavior (using a stubbed SimpleRSS.parse / fakeweb, both of which are available in the Gemfile).

findings.title: Disqus import rewritten to TopicEmbed.import_remote but reply posts are created with raw HTML cooked content and no cook_method
findings.body: The diff replaces the old PostCreator-based topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, then creates reply posts with `attrs = { ..., raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked], ... }` (lines 160-165). The Disqus `message` field is HTML from the export; setting both raw and cooked to that HTML and creating via PostCreator means the post goes through the normal Markdown cook pipeline (cook_method defaults to regular), which will mangle the HTML (Markdown-processed HTML often renders incorrectly), and the before_save callback recomputes cooked from raw anyway. The replies should either be created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (matching the imported topic) or converted to Markdown. As written, imported Disqus replies will be double-processed and likely display broken markup. Also, `Date.parse(p[:created_at])` will raise on malformed dates, aborting the whole import with no error handling.

findings.title: Disqus import creates users from unvalidated author emails with no approval
findings.body: `post_user = User.create!(email: email, username: UserNameSuggester.suggest(email))` creates a full user account for every distinct author email in the Disqus export, with no validation of the email beyond `Email.downcase`, no check against the email blacklist (which is explicitly cleared on line 141: `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist = ""`), and no approval/trust gating. A malicious Disqus export (the import file is operator-supplied, but exports can be crafted) can create thousands of accounts with arbitrary email addresses, which then appear as post authors. These auto-created users have trust level 0 but can still be spam vectors (they exist, can be messaged, appear in user lists). The import should use a dedicated import user or staged/unapproved accounts, and the blacklist should not be globally disabled for the duration.

findings.title: Referer host comparison doesn't handle missing port/scheme normalization and is case-sensitive
findings.body: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` — URI#host returns a downcased host without port, but SiteSetting.embeddable_host is compared as a raw string. If the admin enters `Eviltrout.com` or `eviltrout.com:80` or `http://eviltrout.com` in the setting, the comparison fails for every request and the feature is entirely broken (all requests raise InvalidAccess). The setting should be normalized once (downcase, strip scheme/port) before comparison, or the comparison should parse the setting as a URI too. The spec (embed_controller_spec.rb) only tests with an exact lowercase match, so this misconfiguration is untested.

findings.title: Script assumes #discourse-comments exists; throws if the host page lacks it
findings.body: `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` can return null if the host page doesn't include the expected div (typo, different embed snippet version, CSP-modified DOM), and `comments.appendChild(iframe)` on line 12 then throws a TypeError, breaking the entire script. The embed snippet should be documented as requiring the div, but the script should guard: `if (!comments) { return; }`. Low severity (host-page integration issue), but it silently breaks embedding with no error message.

findings.title: import_remote fetches the full page with no timeout, size limit, or redirect limit
findings.body: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` reads the entire response body into memory with open-uri defaults: no open_timeout/read_timeout, no redirect limit (open-uri follows up to 10 redirects by default), and no maximum size. A slow or huge page on the allowed host (or an allowed-host URL redirecting to a multi-GB file) will hang the Sidekiq worker and consume unbounded memory. The fetch should use explicit timeouts, a redirect cap with re-validation, and a maximum content length.

findings.title: TopicRetriever spec never tests the actual retrieval, throttling, or host validation logic end-to-end
findings.body: All tests mock `perform_retrieve` or `retrieved_recently?`, so the spec verifies only the wiring of `retrieve` (that it calls perform_retrieve unless invalid_host?/retrieved_recently?). It never tests that invalid_host? correctly parses URIs, that retrieved_recently? actually uses Redis setnx/expire correctly (the throttle could be broken and no test would catch it), that perform_retrieve checks TopicEmbed existence, or that fetch_http looks up the embed user. The Redis throttle in particular is concurrency-sensitive logic that deserves a real test (mock_redis is available in the Gemfile).
